title: 3.5 cm x 4.5 cm Photo: Resize Online in Pixels and KB
description: Make a 3.5 × 4.5 cm photo online: 276 × 354 px at 200 DPI or 413 × 531 px at 300 DPI, with an optional KB limit. Free, and your photo stays on your phone.
intro: Need a 3.5 cm × 4.5 cm photo for a form? The size is already filled in. Add your picture, choose 200 or 300 DPI, set a KB limit if the form gives one, and download.

steps.name: Add your photo
steps.text: Pick a recent front-facing picture, ideally taken against a plain light wall in daylight.

steps.name: Choose the DPI
steps.text: 200 DPI suits almost every online form. Pick 300 DPI when the notice asks for it or you plan to print.

steps.name: Add a KB limit
steps.text: If the form says something like "maximum 50 KB", type 50 in Max size. Otherwise leave it empty.

steps.name: Download
steps.text: When the pass check shows ticks for pixels and size, save the JPG.

faq.q: What is 3.5 cm × 4.5 cm in pixels?
faq.a: At 200 DPI it is 276 × 354 pixels; at 300 DPI it is 413 × 531 pixels. The rule is pixels = centimetres ÷ 2.54 × DPI, rounded to whole pixels.

faq.q: Is 4.5 cm × 3.5 cm in pixels any different?
faq.a: No. It is the same photo, just written height first. The photo stands upright: 3.5 cm wide and 4.5 cm tall, so 276 × 354 px at 200 DPI.
No. If your picture has a different shape, the tool trims a little from the edges and keeps the centre, so proportions stay natural. Keep your face in the middle when you take it.
Use the one your notice states. When it gives none, 200 DPI is the usual choice for online forms; the DPI value is also written into the JPG.

sections.h2: Why 3.5 × 4.5 cm has two pixel sizes
paras: A digital image has no centimetres, only pixels. The DPI (dots per inch) links the two, and one inch is 2.54 cm. So 3.5 cm at 200 DPI is 3.5 ÷ 2.54 × 200 ≈ 276 pixels, and 4.5 cm is about 354. At 300 DPI the same photo needs 413 × 531 pixels, which is sharper in print but a larger file.

CTET is one exam that asks for exactly this: a 3.5 × 4.5 cm photo at 200 DPI (276 × 354 px) between 10 and 100 KB. If your exam has a kit on SahiSize, open it instead; the KB range is already set there.

sections.h2: Tips for a photo that gets accepted
paras: Let the face fill most of the frame with both ears visible, look straight at the camera and use a plain white or light background. Avoid caps, dark glasses and beauty filters. Save as JPG, the format nearly every portal accepts.
